name: Business websites
promise: A branded site that represents your business around the clock.
blurb: The core build. Three packages, each a one-time price agreed before I start.
intro: A business website exists to win the minute when someone finds you on their phone and decides whether to call.
The essentials come first: what you do, where you are, what it costs and how to reach you.
Every site is custom-coded, not built from a template, so it loads fast on mobile and stays easy to change.
includes: The pages your package allows, 3, 5 or 7 in total
A contact form that reaches your inbox
Google Maps, hours and click to call
On-page SEO built in, not sold back to you
Hosting, SSL and backups on your care plan
Built for phones first

faq.q: What do you need from me to start?
faq.a: Your logo if you have one, photos of your own work, and a rough idea of what you want each page to say. If you have none of that, content preparation covers me gathering it with you. It is a listed fee between $100 and $175, not a surprise.

faq.q: Who owns the site when it is done?
faq.a: Once the project is paid in full, the final in-scope site is yours. You own the domain outright because you bought it in your own name. The care plan covers hosting and updates, not custody of your own business.

faq.q: Why is a care plan required?
faq.a: A site nobody hosts, backs up or patches is not a working site. The plan starts at $45 a month, covers hosting, SSL, backups and monitoring, and includes edits. There is a 3-month minimum and then you can cancel with 30 days' notice.

name: Menu and services pages
promise: Everything you offer, on one page a customer can actually read.
blurb: Food, nails, detailing, lawn care. Any business with a list.
intro: A photographed PDF menu is unreadable on a phone, invisible to Google and wrong the day a price changes.
A real menu or services page is text. It fits any screen, can be searched, and a price change takes a minute.
Past about 20 items it needs categories and filtering. That is the complex price, and the only thing that moves it.
includes: Every item as real text, not an image of text
Prices you can change without a redesign
Categories and sections once the list is long
Photos per item where you have them
Readable at arm's length on a phone

faq.q: What if I do not sell food?
faq.a: Then it is a services page and it works identically. A lawn care company listing five services and a restaurant listing sixty items are the same page with different amounts in it, which is exactly what simple and complex measure.

faq.q: Can I update the prices myself?
faq.a: Small price changes are covered by the edit allowance on your care plan, so you message me and it is done. If you want to make the changes yourself, self-editable content is a $225 power feature and it is built for exactly this.

blurb: Lead capture for the jobs that need a conversation first.
intro: The biggest jobs need a conversation first, and those enquiries often arrive as a missed call or a message with no detail.
A quote page asks the right questions up front, so you open your inbox to a date, a headcount and a budget.
The complex version also sells: your packages, what each includes, and pricing tiers.

faq.q: How is this different from the contact form?
faq.a: The contact form asks for a name and a message. This one asks the questions that decide whether you can take the job and what to charge for it: the date, the headcount, the specifics. It is the difference between an enquiry and a lead.

faq.q: Does it calculate a price for the customer?
faq.a: No. It collects what you need to respond with a quote, estimate or catering booking - it does not calculate pricing, run a customer-configurable pricing engine, or take a deposit. Catering is this feature's restaurant-specific form; anything past that (full package pricing displayed on the page, payment collection) is quoted separately.

blurb: Calendly, Square, Booksy or Vagaro, wired into the site properly.
intro: Every booking made by phone costs a call, and every missed call costs a booking.
I connect your booking system to your site so people see your real availability, with the booking buttons where they decide.
Deposits or payment at booking are a further $150 on either option. It is the part that stops no-shows.

faq.q: Do I need an account already?
faq.a: No, but having one makes it a standard setup rather than a complex one, and that is one of the things the price measures. If you do not have one, I will set it up and configure your services with you.

faq.q: Which platform should I use?
faq.a: Tell me how you take bookings today and I will tell you plainly. Most single-service businesses are well served by Calendly's free tier; salons and multi-staff operations usually need something like Square or Vagaro.

faq.q: Will you build or run my booking system for me?
faq.a: No. I integrate one provider you already use into the site's customer journey - the main booking destination and the buttons that lead to it. I am not building a scheduling platform or administering your booking system day to day, and that stays yours to run.

name: Logo Design
promise: A custom logo for your business, with two design directions to choose from.
blurb: A custom logo: two design directions, two revision rounds, light and dark versions.
intro: A custom primary logo, designed for your business.
You get two design directions. Pick one, and it is refined through two revision rounds.
It is delivered in light and dark versions as final PNG and SVG files. Want colors, type and social assets around it? That is Brand Identity.

pricing.note: Two design directions and two revision rounds are included. A round is one consolidated list of changes.

turnaroundNote: Timing is agreed when we start. It depends on how quickly you choose a direction and send your revision notes.

faq.q: What kind of logos does this cover?
faq.a: Wordmarks, monograms, typography-based marks and simple geometric or custom symbols. Detailed mascots, hand-drawn illustration and specialized lettering are outside what I do in-house.

faq.q: Can you check that my name and logo are not already trademarked?
faq.a: No. I do not perform trademark searches or trademark clearance, and I cannot tell you a name or mark is free to use. Confirming that it does not infringe existing rights is your responsibility, and an attorney is the right person to ask.

faq.q: Can the files go straight to a printer, sign maker or embroiderer?
faq.a: The files are prepared for digital use and can be a starting point for physical production. I do not supply validated Pantone, CMYK, vinyl, thread or embroidery specifications, so final suitability is confirmed with the vendor through their own proofing process.

name: Care plans
promise: The site stays hosted, secure, backed up and current, without you touching it.
blurb: Required with every build. $45 or $95 a month.
intro: A site with last year's hours and prices does more harm than no site.
A care plan keeps it current and is required with every build. A site nobody hosts, patches or backs up is not a working site.
Host keeps the site online and current. Grow adds monthly work: four updates, faster turnaround and a managed Google Business Profile.
includes: Hosting, SSL and daily backups
Uptime monitoring
Edits handled by me, with no CMS to learn
Google Business Profile management on Grow
A monthly performance report on Grow
3-month minimum, then 30 days' notice

faq.q: What counts as one update?
faq.a: One request, however many small changes are in it. Sending four photos to swap is one update, not four. Host covers up to 15 minutes of edits a month; Grow covers four updates a month with a 3-business-day turnaround.

faq.q: How do I request a change?
faq.a: You message me. You work directly with ALVSolutions, with no ticket queue or outsourced support.

faq.q: What if I need more than my plan covers?
faq.a: Anything beyond the allowance is priced by size and published: $30 minor, $60 moderate, $100 substantial. You will get told which bracket a job lands in before I do it.

faq.q: Can I cancel?
faq.a: After the 3-month minimum, with 30 days' notice. Cancellation takes effect at the end of your current billing period, and that period is not refunded. After that I stop hosting, maintaining and monitoring the site. You get a 30-day handoff window after cancellation takes effect, followed by a 30-day archive window. After the archive window ends I am no longer required to keep archived site files or backups, and recovery is not guaranteed. One basic handoff to a compatible hosting environment is included. Ownership of the finished site transfers to you once the project is paid in full. A complex migration may need a quote you approve first, and any third-party cost is yours.

intro: Your Google Business Profile shows your hours, photos, reviews and a call button above the search results.
I set it up inside your own Google account, so it belongs to you. Categories, service areas, hours, description, photos and the first review request are all handled.
Google controls verification timelines, so I cannot promise a date. I make sure everything is correct the moment it goes live.
includes: Created or claimed in your own Google account

pricing.note: Setup assistance is included in Standard and Complete. Ongoing management, posts and review responses are part of the Grow care plan at $95 a month.

faq.q: Whose account is it in?
faq.a: Yours. I work inside your Google account rather than creating one I control. If we part ways, the listing does not move.

faq.q: How long does verification take?
faq.a: Google decides that, and it ranges from a day to a few weeks depending on how they choose to verify you. I submit it and follow it through, but nobody can promise you a date.

faq.q: Is this SEO?
faq.a: It is the local half of it, and for a business with a service area it is usually the half that brings the phone calls. On-page SEO for the site itself is built into every package at no extra cost.
